shouldFix.title: The newly-precise supersession leaves the superseded COORD text live, unannotated, and with no named later act
shouldFix.finding: Turn 2 correctly narrows the supersession to two specific sentences that remain live, unmarked, inside the adopted D-056 Decision paragraph at COORD 741fdc73 lines 3378-3380. The entry does not say what happens to that text: it names no later recording-hygiene act that would append a forward pointer to D-133, and it does not expressly accept the resulting conflict with reasons. From adoption onward, a reader who lands on D-056 in COORD reads 'DR-103/104/105/114/118 and the twelve no-contract rows remain ineligible' as a flat holding, with nothing at the point of use indicating it has been reduced to a dated measurement. This is not hypothetical reliance: D-131, the most recent adopted recording, demonstrably recites D-056 from that paragraph. The concrete failure mode is the one D-133 exists to prevent — a later cycle that has closed DR-103's fixture-authoring leftover reads the flat sentence, concludes the row is still barred by name, and condition 2 stays stuck. D-056's own pinned subject set the contrary norm in its Decision 2: 'Two authorities will not remain in conflict at the moment of that re-record: the re-record's MF-6 edit is what removes the cell-level bar.' The corpus has repaired this exact class of defect repeatedly under freeze §7.10 and the pin-move records: text that has moved must say so where it is read, not only where it was moved.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: Nothing in the entry is false or unlawful, the supersession is properly named and scoped, and the overturn path is coherent. This is an incompleteness in the recording plan, not a defect in the decision.
shouldFix.whyThisIsNewAtTurn2: Turn 1 superseded 'D-056's closed eligible-in-kind name list' as a generality, which pointed at no specific live bytes. Turn 2 supersedes two exact sentences that stay in place. The precision I demanded is what creates the point-of-use gap, so this is a consequence of the accepted repair rather than a re-litigation of it.
shouldFix.repair: One sentence, either branch. (a) Name the follow-on act: a later recording-hygiene entry, its own cycle and commit, appends a forward annotation to the COORD D-056 Decision paragraph recording that its two name-list sentences are dated 2026-08-14 measurements held by D-133 and that the pinned turn-2 subject's five gates govern — stated as owed work here, performed there. Or (b) expressly accept the unannotated conflict and say why it is tolerable, so the next reader of D-056 is not misled by silence. Either discharges this; leaving the question unasked does not.

Custody is intact: turn-2 subject 4292 2837 at 0444 unmoved, turn-1 subject frozen at e548bd46, HEAD never left d3efe3c, governing tree clean, and all eight measured-inputs rows reproduce exactly including both turn-1 verdict files. D-131 demonstrably reads D-056 from that paragraph, so the failure mode is concrete — a later cycle that closes DR-103's leftover reads a flat by-name bar and condition 2 stays stuck, which is the harm D-133 exists to prevent. Everything else in the entry is correct and should carry into turn 3 unchanged.
